The stack grew out of <jad>JAD</jad> and: The stack grew out of JAD and runs {count} Docker Compose services, profiles included: infrastructure (Traefik, PostgreSQL, Vault, NATS, Keycloak), EDC 1.0 (the control plane, with siglet as its data plane, ADR-078), identity (Identity Hub, Issuer Service), application (Neo4j, proxy, UI) and a static GitHub Pages export. The same topology runs on Azure Container Apps at {host} (ADR-012); the apps there are the ones the off-hours script stops and starts. Arrows show runtime dependencies.
The Azure deployment runs Monday to Frid: The Azure deployment runs Monday to Friday, 05:17 to 18:13 UTC, and is stopped outside those hours (ADR-053); two Container Apps jobs trigger the stop and the start (ADR-058). Stopping is a real stop through the Container Apps API, not scale-to-zero, because nearly every service is called by another one and would never reach zero replicas. The UI is the exception: it sleeps at zero replicas, wakes for a visitor and serves an offline notice that links the static export.
<hol>Berlin public holidays</hol> skip t: Berlin public holidays skip the start. The catalog crawler runs in office hours only. A night or weekend session holds the stack with the repository variable LIVE_DEMO_HOLD_UNTIL; see the off-hours runbook.

The <dsp>Dataspace Protocol</dsp> (DSP): The <dsp>Dataspace Protocol</dsp> (DSP) governs how data holders and data users negotiate access to health datasets. The EHDS regulation adds <hdab>HDAB approval</hdab> as a pre-requisite for <permit>data permit</permit> issuance before contract negotiation can proceed.
DSP contract negotiation as a sequence d: DSP contract negotiation as a sequence diagram: the user queries the catalogue, applies to the access body and receives the permit as a credential, then negotiates the contract with the holder, who verifies the permit and evaluates the policy before agreeing and transferring the data

The <dcp>Decentralized Claims Protocol</: The <dcp>Decentralized Claims Protocol</dcp> (DCP) manages identity, credentials, and trust. <ih>Identity Hub</ih> stores DIDs and Verifiable Credentials, the Issuer Service mints EHDS-specific credentials, and <kc>Keycloak</kc> provides SSO/<oidc>OIDC</oidc> authentication.
Identity and trust as an ArchiMate appli: Identity and trust as an ArchiMate application cooperation view: the trust anchors, the DCP identity layer with Identity Hub, Issuer Service and the Secure Token Service, the five credentials the issuer defines, and the interfaces the tokens protect
The hub and the EU's Simpl-Open middlewa: The hub and the EU's Simpl-Open middleware stand on the same foundation: both run Eclipse EDC connectors, speak the Dataspace Protocol and admit participants with credentials from an authority they trust. The hub joins a Simpl data space as an EDC connector outside the Simpl-Open agent (<adr>ADR-064</adr>) and brings what health adds on top: FHIR and OMOP semantics, data permits, the right to opt out (<art71>Art. 71</art71>), fees and the gate in front of the secure processing environments.
